title: Nehemiah Bible Quiz - Chapter 13
description: Ten questions on Nehemiah 13: Nehemiah returns to Jerusalem and deals with Tobiah's room, the tithes, the Sabbath and foreign marriages.

questions.text: What was found written in the book of Moses about the assembly of God?
questions.explanation: It was found written that an Ammonite and a Moabite should not enter into the assembly of God forever.

answers.text: An Edomite and an Egyptian should not enter it
An Ammonite and a Moabite should not enter it
A Philistine and a Canaanite should not enter it
A Hittite and an Amorite should not enter it

questions.text: Whom did they hire to curse the children of Israel?
questions.explanation: They did not meet Israel with bread and water, but hired Balaam to curse them; God turned the curse into a blessing.

questions.text: For whom had Eliashib the priest prepared a great room in the house of God?
questions.explanation: Eliashib, who was allied to Tobiah, had prepared a great room for him where the offerings used to be kept.

questions.text: What did the narrator do when he understood what had been done for Tobiah?
questions.explanation: He understood the evil Eliashib had done for Tobiah; it grieved him severely, so he threw all Tobiah's household stuff out of the room.

answers.text: He burned the room and everything in it
He gave the room to the singers instead
He threw out all Tobiah's household stuff
He sealed the door of the room with stones

questions.text: What had the Levites and singers done because their portions had not been given?
questions.explanation: The portions of the Levites had not been given them, so each of them had fled to his field.

answers.text: They had gone back to Babylon
Each had fled to his field
They had gone to the king

questions.text: What did the men of Tyre bring in and sell on the Sabbath?
questions.explanation: Men of Tyre brought in fish and all kinds of wares and sold on the Sabbath to the children of Judah.

answers.text: Fish and all kinds of wares

questions.text: When did the narrator command the doors of Jerusalem to be shut?
questions.explanation: When the gates began to be dark before the Sabbath, he commanded the doors shut until after the Sabbath.

answers.text: At midday on the Sabbath itself
Only on the days of the feasts
As it grew dark before the Sabbath

questions.text: In whose speech did half of the children of the mixed marriages speak?
questions.explanation: Their children spoke half in the speech of Ashdod and could not speak in the Jews' language.

questions.text: Which king of Israel does the text say foreign women caused to sin?
questions.explanation: Solomon king of Israel, who was loved by his God, was caused to sin by foreign women.

questions.text: One of the sons of Joiada was son-in-law to whom?
questions.explanation: One of the sons of Joiada, the son of Eliashib the high priest, was son-in-law to Sanballat the Horonite, so the narrator chased him away.
